question: What share of exploited vulnerabilities in 2025-2026 were found or weaponized by AI/LLM systems vs humans, and how fast (disclosure -> exploit) for middle-tier servers (web servers, proxies, gateways, app frameworks)? Does the R-THR-2 SLA scope (<=24 h own attacker-reachable code, <=7 d Tier-S deps, <=6 h drill target) hold?
flips_if: q1-009 shows AI-found bugs are exploited above the base rate (then the <=24 h SLA becomes a rule for all TCB code) [ARCHITECTURE §2.3 reverse].

measured.ai_found_exploitation_rate: 14 of 1,061 AI-attributed CVEs confirmed exploited = 1.3% (Wilson 95% CI 0.8-2.2%), vs all-CVE KEV ratio 1.4% in 1H 2026 and ~1% of 2025 CVEs exploited by year end (VulnCheck 1H 2026; 2026 Exploit Intelligence Report). Glasswing: >23,000 findings -> 126 CVEs -> 1 exploited (Ghost CMS SQLi CVE-2026-26980); later VulnCheck tracking 225 Anthropic/Glasswing-linked CVEs, still 1 exploited (as of 2026-09-21). AI-found = base rate, not above. Grade B.
measured.ai_share_of_exploited: Lower bound ~2.8% of 1H 2026 KEVs (14 AI-attributed exploited / 495 KEVs; Wilson 1.7-4.7%; windows not perfectly aligned). Middle-tier KEV sample: 1 of 35 2025+ CVEs credited to an AI-based auditing firm (CVE-2026-34486 Tomcat, striga.ai) = 2.9% (Wilson 0.5-14.5%). Most middle-tier KEVs are appliance zero-days with no public finder credit, so the true AI share is unknown above this floor. Grade B (floor) / D (ceiling).
measured.ai_weaponization: Documented, not quantifiable: Erlang/OTP SSH CVE-2025-32433 public PoC written with GPT-4 from the patch diff within ~1 day of 2025-04-16 disclosure (human-found bug); GTIG 2026-05-11 first in-the-wild exploit assessed as AI-developed (2FA logic bypass in an open-source web admin tool; stopped before mass use); APT45 recursive CVE analysis + PoC validation with LLMs; Anthropic Sept 2026 report: GTG-10007 AI firmware hunting -> >12 possible appliance zero-days/month (self-reported, unverified). Lab ceiling: CVE-Genie reproduces 428/841 (51%) 2024-25 CVEs at $2.77 each; Auto Exploit 14 OSS CVEs in 10-15 min. Counter-signal: most public AI PoCs are non-functional 'slop' (React2Shell first PoC; VulnCheck). No source gives a share of exploited CVEs weaponized by AI. Grade C.
measured.speed_all_kev: 28.96% of 2025 KEVs exploited on/before CVE publication day (VulnCheck, 884 KEVs); 23.43% in 1H 2026 (495 KEVs); median CVE->KEV 120 d (2025) -> 80 d (1H 2026). Mandiant M-Trends 2026: mean time-to-exploit -7 days (2025 incidents). Grade A/B.
measured.speed_middle_tier_measured: CISA KEV catalog 2026.10.23, entries added >=2025-01-01 in web server/proxy/ADC/gateway/app-framework products, CVE date from cvelistV5: n=41 (35 with 2025+ CVEs). For the 35: day-0 (KEV same day as CVE) 12 = 34% (CI 21-51%); <=2 d 15 = 43% (28-59%); <=7 d 18 = 51% (36-67%); <=30 d 23 = 66%; median 7 d. Split: appliance/commercial n=25 median 1 d, 11 day-0 (state/criminal zero-days in Citrix, Fortinet, Ivanti, Check Point, F5); OSS n=10 median 42.5 d by KEV date, but KEV lags reality: first exploitation was hours after disclosure for React2Shell CVE-2025-55182 (AWS), ~30 h for Tomcat CVE-2025-24813 (Wallarm), 36 h after GHSA indexing for LiteLLM CVE-2026-42208 (Sysdig). KEV dateAdded is an upper bound on first exploitation. Grade A (measurement) / B (first-exploitation anecdotes).
measured.buyer_patch_window: ASD ISM-1876/1877: patch internet-facing services within 48 h when critical or a working exploit exists (q4-003 corpus), so a vendor release must land well inside 48 h to be usable.

decision_effect: R-THR-2 scope: the reverse condition does NOT fire. AI-found bugs are exploited at the base rate (1.3% vs 1.4%), so do not extend the <=24 h SLA to all TCB code on AI grounds. Keep: <=24 h private report/advisory -> signed release for aegis-canon, the transport wrapper and H1 framing; <=6 h advisory -> TUF release as the quarterly drill target (still E until the drill runs). Its justification is disclosure-to-exploit speed (hours to ~2 days for high-profile OSS middle-tier bugs; 43% of middle-tier KEVs <=2 d) and the 48 h buyer patch window (ASD ISM-1877), not AI discovery. TIGHTEN one row, on speed evidence independent of AI: Tier-S dependency with a published fix that is pre-auth network-reachable through AEGIS (critical or KEV-listed) -> <=48 h to signed golden rebuild (was <=7 d); keep <=7 d for other Tier-S dependency fixes. Rationale: observed OSS middle-tier first exploitation at 30-48 h after disclosure, and 51% of middle-tier KEVs within 7 d, so a 7-day rebuild lands after the median. Add to §2.1 AA1-skeptic: 'AI raises finding volume (Glasswing 23k findings; CVE-Genie 51% repro at $2.77) and PoC noise, not the per-CVE exploitation rate; the operative risk is time-to-exploit, which is driven by zero-day use against appliances and by hours-scale n-day weaponization of high-profile OSS.' The kill-switch row stays: about a third of middle-tier exploitation is at or before disclosure, where no rebuild SLA helps.
rung: Measurement grade B overall (KEV-lag computation A; AI attribution B floor / D ceiling; weaponization share C).
reproduce: curl -sL -o kev.json https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json && python3 -I spikes/q1-009/raw/kevmid.py kev.json out.json   (catalogVersion 2026.10.23 gives: CVE published 2025+ n 35 median 7 day0 12 <=2d 15 <=7d 18 <=30d 23; OSS n 10; appliance n 25). VulnCheck figures: https://wwv.vulncheck.com/hubfs/Research/State-of-Exploitation-1H-2026.pdf and https://wwv.vulncheck.com/hubfs/Research/2026-VulnCheck-Exploit-Intelligence-Report.pdf (pdftotext; pages 11-13 and 13/17).
limits: AI attribution relies on public credits (Anthropic-credited list + Berkeley initiative), which miss attacker-side AI use entirely; attacker-found zero-days have no finder credit, so 'AI share of exploited' has only a floor. KEV dateAdded is a lagging upper bound on first exploitation; CVE datePublished can lag GHSA/vendor advisories (LiteLLM CVE-2026-42208 shows lag 0 but was exploited before its CVE record date). Middle-tier product selection is a manual vendor/product filter (41 entries) and may omit products listed under generic names. Time-to-exploit for OSS uses vendor/honeypot anecdotes (AWS, Wallarm, Sysdig), not a systematic dataset. Glasswing/Anthropic numbers are partly self-reported. The trend could change quickly as frontier cyber models spread (VulnCheck and GTIG both flag this). Re-run each half-year with the new VulnCheck report.
